docs.purpose: The full-screen message a user meets when their free trial has run out. It tells them how many jobs they viewed during the trial and offers a button that opens a checkout page in a browser. They can also dismiss it and keep browsing with everything blurred out. If they have already paid and nothing has changed, a link appears after a minute to re-check their status.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/subscribe/session`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `entitlements` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `subscribe_nonces`. It also holds client-side state in `paywallStore`, which is the part a server-driven projection has to absorb or justify.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it holds Layer-3 state (`paywallStore`) and drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading by reference: `/api/subscribe/session`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/paywall/PaywallScreen.tsx`.

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: The checkout response is parsed by SubscribeSessionResponseSchema against a server type file the hook names by path; the comment at useSubscribeCheckout.ts:25 spells out that the server type must change first.

inputs.why: Its only render input is the leadViewsCount prop the tab shell passes from the already-fetched profile; the checkout contract is outbound, fired on tap.

outputs.why: Tapping the CTA POSTs /api/subscribe/session, which mints a single-use nonce row and returns a web checkout URL; the app then opens the system browser and waits for the webhook plus the AppState re-fetch — it never marks itself paid.
outputs.rollback: none — the nonce is server-minted and single-use; a failed open sets a typed local error and fires the error haptic rather than undoing anything.

state.why: It owns paywallStore.dismissed, which is deliberately NOT persisted so a returning user meets the full paywall again rather than the inline blur.

staleness.why: The status it exists to react to is the shared 5-minute ["user-profile"] entry; the 60-second "Refresh status" link is a manual invalidate for the webhook-delay case.

session.why: Only an authenticated user can reach it (the tab shell mounts it), and /api/subscribe/session is under the explicitly-listed /api/subscribe authenticated prefix — the sibling /api/subscribe/exchange is the exact-match public exception.

rls_class.why: It reads its own user_profiles/entitlements rows and mints its own subscribe_nonces row — all Class A, owner-scoped on auth.uid(), with subscribe_nonces carrying select/insert/delete policies because exchange consumes by DELETE.

guards.flag: EXPO_PUBLIC_PAYWALL_CTA_NEUTRAL (PaywallScreen.tsx:39 — swaps the CTA copy for the App Store Guideline 3.1.1 case)
guards.rate_bucket: none — /api/subscribe/session calls no withRateLimit; the FOR UPDATE row lock is what serialises concurrent taps

checks.why: mobile/__tests__/paywallStore.test.ts pins the dismiss/reset transitions the tab shell branches on.
Spec 96 §9 is explicit that dismissal must not survive a relaunch; paywallStore is a plain create() with no persist middleware, unlike every other store in the app.
The mount fade sets pointerEvents="none" until the withTiming completion callback fires through runOnJS, so a fast-tapping user cannot fire the CTA mid-fade (app/(app)/_layout.tsx:92-111).
paywall_shown and subscribe_button_clicked are production events; paywall_dismissed is DEV-only by the §7.3 frequency-split rule, so the dismissal rate is not measurable in production.
leadViewsCount === 0 renders alternative copy instead of "0 leads", which matters because that counter is structurally zero for every mobile user (see limitations).

errors.why: Closest legal value, and a stretch: a failed checkout produces an error HAPTIC and nothing visual at all — transient like a toast, keeping the previous content, but with no message. The typed error useSubscribeCheckout stores is never read by this surface.

classes.ui: already_active — no visible message; the error haptic fires and the CTA stays.
unknown — captured to Sentry, then the same silent haptic.
NetworkError — same silent haptic; the "Refresh status" link is the only recovery affordance.

emits.why: Three funnel events — shown, CTA tapped (fired on tap, before the async resolves, so it measures intent), and dismissed (DEV-only); no ledger row is written because no usage ledger table exists.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: Its one tunable, the 60-second refresh reveal, is a module constant (REVEAL_REFRESH_AFTER_MS) rather than a registered logic variable.

sharing.why: POST /api/subscribe/session is rendered by this surface and nothing else in the mobile estate.

limitations.what: The headline number — "N leads viewed in your 14-day trial" — is structurally zero for every mobile user, because the only writer of lead_views_count has no mobile caller.
limitations.measured: user_profiles.lead_views_count is incremented only at src/app/api/leads/view/route.ts:110; its hook src/features/leads/api/useLeadView.ts is imported only by src/tests/useLeadView.logic.test.tsx; no file under mobile/ references /api/leads/view.

limitations.what: A failed checkout tells the user nothing: the typed error from useSubscribeCheckout is never rendered on this screen.
limitations.measured: PaywallScreen.tsx:44 destructures only { openCheckout, isLoading }; the hook's `error` field is read by the settings billing row but not here.

limitations.what: Five staggered entry animations plus the 400ms refresh reveal run regardless of the OS reduce-motion setting.
limitations.measured: PaywallScreen.tsx:57-86 — withDelay/withTiming in mount effects; no AccessibilityInfo call exists in mobile/.
limitations.check_id: none — checks[].kind has no reduced-motion value; raised as a vocabulary escalation per Spec 128 §4

notes: This is a GATE whose entitlement statuses are the INVERSE of every other gated surface: it renders precisely when status is expired. The checkout is a web hand-off — the nonce in the URL is the credential, which is why /api/subscribe/exchange is an exact-match public path while its siblings stay authenticated.

programme.why: The subscription and Stripe hand-off, which resolves an entitlement per PRODUCT — so it serves both and belongs to neither.

leakage.behaviour: Renders trial copy from `user_profiles.lead_views_count` — a lead-gen counter — on a paywall that also stands in front of the parcel product. The counter is structurally 0 (its only writer has no caller), so every trial user sees the zero-state copy regardless of which product they came from.

product_questions.question: Should the trial paywall tell a parcel-tool user how many LEADS they have viewed? The copy is lead-gen framing on a gate that also stands in front of the parcel product.
product_questions.measured: The `{N} leads` branch is unreachable in production because the counter never increments, so every trial user sees the zero-state copy — which hides the question rather than answering it.
product_questions.spec_says: Spec 95 §2.2.1 designs the trial view counter. Spec 128 R-08 retires the meter in favour of `usage_events`, which makes this copy a product decision rather than a bug fix.
